text.text:
We have been customers for more than 10 years, and every time we traveled from Fresno, CA, this restaurant was one of our must-stop places. We always enjoyed the great food, welcoming atmosphere, and friendly service that made it special.

Unfortunately, during our most recent visits, we have noticed a significant decline in quality since Eduardo is no longer involved with the business. I ordered a lomito sandwich that cost $17, and honestly, it looked more like a Subway sandwich—mostly lettuce and tomato, with very little meat. It was not what we had come to expect from this restaurant.

In addition, the manager came across as arrogant, standing behind the employees and watching them constantly, which created an uncomfortable atmosphere.

We sincerely hope the restaurant can regain the quality, simplicity, and warm hospitality that made it one of our favorite places for so many years. It would be a shame to see it lose what once made it so special.

As someone from Tijuana, Baja California, I’m always on the hunt for great chilaquiles. I visited Farm Table today with high expectations because I love seeing restaurants incorporate Mexican flavors into their menu.

The atmosphere was beautiful (10/10), and the presentation of the dish was excellent (10/10). The service was good overall (7/10). Unfortunately, the chilaquiles didn’t meet my expectations (4/10). The tortilla chips were much too soggy instead of having that crispy texture, and the sauce was a bit overpowering, making it difficult to enjoy the other flavors.

For me, Garcia Bros Cafe still takes the top spot for authentic flavor, quality, and texture. If you’re looking for excellent customer service and consistently delicious food, I highly recommend Garcia Bros Cafe.

It has been over 20 years since I last stepped foot inside a Sizzler, but decided to give them another try this past weekend when I was up in the valley. I was pleasantly surprised of how good it was. Basically it’s a smaller version of Soup Plantation but I think much better than Red Lobster and other chains. The shrimp at Sizzled is actually better than Red Lobster, they just have the cheddar biscuits.

This location works by you place your order at the counter and then opt to add salad bar or not. The salad bar is only $12 so it’s a really fair deal and it comes with all sorts of options as well as tacos and a dessert station. For my meal I ordered the New York steak and thought it was pretty good. It’s not like a premium steakhouse, but it does taste like a really decent steak that you would purchase at the grocery store and cook yourself. It was not too fatty and I really enjoyed it. It is a bit expensive compared to the average lunch and is a lot of food so I would not suggest it for an everyday meal, but I definitely will give Sizzler another chance again in the future and would suggest to others looking for a good mini buffet option.

We found Corner Grille years ago, and it has been amazing every single time. It’s such a unique Korean-Mexican fusion spot — flavors you truly won’t find anywhere else. The combination sounds unexpected, but somehow it works perfectly.

We’ve tried a few different items over the years, but the Chicken Korean Fries are our absolute favorite every time. Nothing like it exists. The flavors are bold, layered, slightly sweet, savory, and just combined so deliciously. It’s one of those dishes you crave again and again.

It’s definitely a hole-in-the-wall spot in a small shopping center — super unassuming — but don’t let that fool you. It’s 100% a must-try. Some of the best, most unique food is always hiding in places like this.

If you’re looking for something different and seriously delicious, put this on your list. We’ll keep coming back.
